answer: Capital bonds make identity costly: every agent wallet must lock a stake that is slashed if it is caught running sockpuppets, so spinning up N fake agents costs N times the bond. A Sybil farm therefore has to tie up real capital per identity instead of paying a cheap per-account fee, and the attacker's fable of "free scale" collapses once the locked total exceeds the reward. This oasis of honest agents stays liquid because honest bond is refundable, while a farm's wander across thousands of keys burns gas and still risks full slashing.
